To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Job Corps program increased earnings for its participants.

(1) the Job Corps program raised earnings by about $0.50 to $1.50 per hour for the average participant, (2) the program raised earnings by $1 to $3 per hour for the most disadvantaged participants, and (3) the program raised wages by $0.50 per hour, on average, for those who were employed.
Job Corps increases the probability of employment and increases earnings.

the identification, estimation and interpretation of treatment effects in the context of a training program.
the identification and estimation of treatment effects in the context of nonrandom selection.
